summary: Refactor where the user reversed an earlier decision; committed partial work plus a dirty in-flight script.

facts.fact: Goal: move notes-cli storage from a JSON file to SQLite (because of slowness and write races).
User constraint: stdlib sqlite3 only; no ORM and no SQLAlchemy.
Final decision (it reversed an earlier one): no --backend flag and no dual-backend Store protocol. Do a one-time migration, then SQLite is the only backend and JsonStore gets removed.
Storing tags as a comma-separated column was tried and abandoned because tags can contain commas; a note_tags join table is used instead.
Surprise: a SQLite DB on /mnt/c (WSL) gives 'database is locked', so the DB lives at ~/.local/share/notes/notes.db.
Done and committed: SqliteStore with the note_tags join table; tests/test_store.py passes.
In flight (uncommitted): scripts/migrate_json.py inserts notes but doesn't migrate tags yet (there's a TODO at the insert loop).
After the migration works: delete JsonStore and point the CLI at SqliteStore directly.
Open question, blocked on the user: after migrating, should notes.json be deleted, renamed to .bak, or left alone? The user will decide; don't pick.
Deferred to a later PR: export.to_csv doesn't quote fields, so commas or quotes in titles break the CSV.

traps.trap: Plans to add or keep a --backend flag or a dual-backend Store protocol.
Proposes storing tags as a comma-separated column.
Decides on its own what happens to notes.json (delete, rename, or keep) as settled.
Includes the CSV quoting fix in the current next step.
